summary: Integrate PentestAgent (https://github.com/GH05TCREW/pentestagent) — an AI agent framework for black-box security testing — into the Namias portfolio to achieve top-tier security posture. Deliverables include automated reconnaissance playbooks, vulnerability scanning, API security testing, CI/CD security gates, remediation of all findings, code-level hardening, and a comprehensive security dashboard showcasing the portfolio as a capstone security engineering project.
narrative: The Namias portfolio is a Next.js App Router marketing site with 50+ components, 6 API routes (chat, resume, media, sanity webhook, sanity live, draft-mode), Sanity CMS integration, Cal.com booking embeds, and Umami analytics. With this growing surface area, a proactive security posture is essential — not just defensive hardening (rate limiting, input sanitisation, env hygiene) but continuous automated black-box testing via PentestAgent. PentestAgent is a Python-based AI agent framework that orchestrates LLM-driven security agents for reconnaissance, vulnerability scanning, exploitation, and reporting. This slice installs PentestAgent, creates the configuration, writes custom playbooks for the portfolio's attack surface, runs the scans, remediates every finding hardens the codebase at the source level, and integrates the results into CI/CD and a security dashboard. The deliverable is a reference-grade security programme that hiring managers can inspect as proof of the owner's security engineering skills.
principles: Defence in depth — PentestAgent complements existing rate-limiting, input sanitisation, and env hygiene from the Security-Hardening branch.
Every finding is a commit — scan results, remediation commits, and re-verification each get their own commit for auditability.
Playbooks are reusable — each PentestAgent playbook targets a specific attack vector and can be re-run on demand.
CI is the enforcement point — automated scans run on every PR and on a schedule; failures block merges.
Document the journey — the security dashboard shows the full posture, not just the final score.
No behaviour change without verification — every remediation is verified by re-running the relevant scan.
Code hardening is layered — middleware-level protections complement application-level input validation.
Security is part of the portfolio brand — the website itself demonstrates security engineering excellence.

personas.label: PP Namias (owner)
goals: Demonstrate top-tier security engineering by making the portfolio itself the capstone project.
Have automated security scans that prove the site is hardened against OWASP Top 10 vectors.
Showcase a security dashboard that hiring managers can inspect.
Achieve 95+ posture score with zero critical vulnerabilities.
painPointsToday: No automated security scanning beyond npm audit.
No black-box testing against the live site.
No security dashboard or posture score to show.
No code-level security middleware for headers, CSP, or cookies.

personas.label: OpenCode / future coding agent
goals: Read a single SKILL.md and know how to run, read, and fix PentestAgent findings.
Be able to re-run any scan playbook and interpret the results.
Know which findings are fixable and which require architectural changes.
Understand the security middleware stack and how to extend it.
painPointsToday: No baseline scan results to compare against.
No list of acceptable vs blocked playbook patterns.

personas.label: Hiring manager / security reviewer
goals: See a comprehensive security dashboard with scan results, posture score, and fix commit history.
Click into any finding and see the remediation commit.
Trust that the security programme is real (not just documentation).
Inspect code-level security controls (middleware, headers, CSP).
painPointsToday: No visible security posture signal in the repo.
Hard to distinguish between documented intentions and actual security controls.
No way to verify the site is tested regularly.
No evidence of proactive security engineering at the code level.

primary: Every OWASP Top 10 category is covered by at least one PentestAgent playbook.
All API endpoints pass black-box testing with zero high-severity findings.
A scheduled CI workflow runs PentestAgent scans weekly and posts results as a CI artifact.
A security dashboard exists at docs/security/dashboard.md showing posture score and fix history.
HTTP security headers middleware is implemented and verified.
CSP is configured with no unsafe-inline in production.
Rate limiting middleware protects all API routes.
secondary: Each playbook has a documented runbook in docs/security/playbooks/.
All findings are tracked in a findings ledger with status, severity, and fix commit.
The security.txt file is deployed at /.well-known/security.txt.
README has visible security posture badges.
A machine-readable security.json endpoint is available.
demo: Local: pentestagent run -t https://namias.tech --playbook portfolio_recon yields structured findings.
CI: A PR with a deliberate security regression is blocked by the PentestAgent check.
Dashboard: docs/security/dashboard.md shows green/amber/red per category with history.
Headers: curl -I https://namias.tech shows CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, etc.

antiPatterns: Running PentestAgent against production without proper rate-limiting safeguards — scans must respect robots.txt and use reasonable delays.
Committing API keys or secrets in PentestAgent config files — all secrets go in .env.
Silencing findings without fixing them — every legitimate finding must have a corresponding remediation commit.
Touching production data during scans — scans run against the live site but only use GET/HEAD for recon and safe POST payloads for API testing.
PentestAgent findings becoming stale — scans must be re-runnable and results timestamped.
Adding security headers without testing their impact on functionality.
Rate limiting that blocks legitimate users — limits must account for normal usage patterns.

epics.title: Advanced attack surface playbooks
epics.summary: Create additional PentestAgent playbooks for advanced attack vectors not covered in EPIC-1 through EPIC-4: clickjacking, open redirect, prototype pollution, host header injection, cache poisoning, and client-side validation bypass.

stories.title: Create clickjacking_testing playbook
stories.details: Write clickjacking_testing.yaml — tests X-Frame-Options and CSP frame-ancestors directives. Sends payloads with X-Frame-Options: DENY, SAMEORIGIN, ALLOW-FROM. Verifies frame-ancestors in CSP. Tests for clickjacking via transparent overlays and drag-and-drop exfiltration.

stories.title: Create open_redirect_testing playbook
stories.details: Write open_redirect_testing.yaml — tests all URL parameters and paths that accept redirect targets: next, redirect, return, url, callback, destination. Tests protocol manipulation, double-slash bypass, CRLF injection, and whitelist bypass via parameter pollution.

stories.title: Create prototype_pollution playbook
stories.details: Write prototype_pollution.yaml — tests for client-side prototype pollution in JS libraries: merge operations, object.assign clones, jQuery.extend. Tests payloads: __proto__, constructor.prototype, JSON.parse merge. Checks for server-side pollution in API JSON parsers.

stories.title: Create host_header_injection playbook
stories.details: Write host_header_injection.yaml — tests Host header manipulation: arbitrary Host, X-Forwarded-Host injection, X-Forwarded-Proto downgrade, absolute URL injection in Host. Checks for password reset poisoning, cache poisoning via Host, and SSRF via Host-controlled redirects.

stories.title: Create cache_poisoning playbook
stories.details: Write cache_poisoning.yaml — tests for web cache poisoning: unkeyed headers (X-Forwarded-Host, X-Original-URL), cookie-based poisoning, response header manipulation via unkeyed query params. Checks Vercel edge cache behaviour.

stories.title: Create client_side_bypass playbook
stories.details: Write client_side_bypass.yaml — tests client-side validation bypass: disabling JS, intercepting/modifying API responses, manipulating localStorage/sessionStorage, bypassing input maxlength via curl, bypassing disabled attributes, testing hidden field manipulation.

stories.title: Document advanced attack surface findings
stories.details: Run all EPIC-9 playbooks and document findings in docs/security/pentestagent/findings/advanced-attack-surface.md.

epics.title: Code-level security hardening
epics.summary: Implement source code hardening: HTTP security headers middleware, CSP configuration, rate limiting, input validation, CSRF protection, cookie hardening, and removal of sensitive data from client bundles. Each change is a separate commit with verification.

stories.title: Harden CSP in next.config.ts
stories.details: Update next.config.ts Content-Security-Policy: add upgrade-insecure-requests, tighten form-action to self, restrict frame-ancestors, add base-uri self, enforce strict-dynamic where possible. Remove unsafe-inline for production builds. Verify with csp_analysis playbook.

stories.title: Add HTTP security headers middleware
stories.details: Create src/middleware.ts (if not exists) or extend existing middleware to set: Strict-Transport-Security (max-age=63072000, includeSubDomains, preload), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy (camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()), X-DNS-Prefetch-Control: off.

stories.title: Harden cookie configuration
stories.details: Audit all Set-Cookie headers in API routes and add: Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax/Strict, __Host- prefix where applicable. Verify __Secure- prefix for cookies set over HTTPS. Document in cookie_security playbook.

stories.title: Add rate limiting middleware for API routes
stories.details: Implement token-bucket or sliding-window rate limiter in middleware.ts for all /api/* routes. Configure limits: /api/chat (10 req/min), /api/resume (30 req/min), /api/media (60 req/min). Return 429 with Retry-After header. Verify with rate_limit_testing playbook.

stories.title: Add input validation for chat endpoint
stories.details: Add Zod schema validation to /api/chat: max message length (2000 chars), allowed HTML (none), allowed markdown (safe subset), block script tags, block javascript: URLs, sanitize with DOMPurify-compatible server-side sanitizer. Verify with xss_testing playbook.

stories.title: Add CSRF protection for webhook endpoint
stories.details: Implement double-submit cookie pattern or custom header validation for /api/sanity/webhook. Verify Sanity webhook secret using timing-safe comparison. Add request body size limits. Verify with csrf_testing playbook.

stories.title: Add request validation middleware for API routes
stories.details: Create reusable Zod validation middleware: content-type check (reject non-JSON), body size limits (100KB max), JSON depth limits (20 levels), reject null bytes in strings, reject prototype pollution keys. Apply to all API routes via middleware chain.

stories.title: Remove sensitive data from client bundles
stories.details: Audit src/ for client components that expose: env vars via NEXT_PUBLIC_*, internal endpoint URLs, API key prefixes, debug info. Remove or isolate. Verify with sensitive_data_exposure playbook.

stories.title: Fix npm dependency vulnerabilities
stories.details: Run npm audit, fix all auto-fixable advisories. For non-auto-fixable: override versions in package.json, document risk. Run npm audit again to verify. Verify with dependency_check playbook.

stories.title: Add security headers verification endpoint
stories.details: Create /api/security-headers endpoint that returns the current security header configuration as JSON. Use for monitoring and verification. Include CSP, HSTS, and other headers in response.
